beats.narration_text: Hallo. This is Liam, in for Bear. A character jump is a movement policy you design. A falling crate asks the solver to handle motion. Mixing those responsibilities makes both harder to tune. We will choose an owner for every motion.

beats.narration_text: A scene organizes an object. Collision defines its boundary and filtering. A movement policy decides what happens over time. Keep those responsibilities separate, and a missing pickup becomes a testable question instead of a mysterious physics bug.

beats.narration_text: Move and slide consumes the velocity property and applies the timestep internally. Move and collide takes a displacement, often velocity times delta. Mixing these contracts is a common source of tiny movement or wildly incorrect speed.

beats.narration_text: A character body gives your code collision and sliding helpers. It does not supply your game's gravity or friction policy. Set velocity in pixels per second, then call move and slide once in the physics callback.

props.title: minimal · source excerpt
props.code:
func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void:
    if not accept_input:
        return
    step(delta, Input.get_axis("move_left", "move_right"),
        Input.is_action_just_pressed("jump"), Input.is_action_just_released("jump"))

# Also executed: godot/player.gd:42
    move_and_slide()

beats.narration_text: Choose jump height and time to the apex. Under constant upward-phase acceleration, gravity is twice the height divided by time squared. Initial upward speed is gravity times apex time. Godot's downward-positive axis makes jump velocity negative.

lecture.why: The spatial or temporal transformation is the claim; a physical-object metaphor would obscure its exact geometry.

beats.narration_text: The reference controller computes rise gravity from those design values. It increases gravity while falling and clamps fall speed. That creates a deliberate game feel. These parameters describe a policy, not an attempt at a universal realistic jump.

lecture.why: Exact runnable source is the teaching target; a full editor layout would reduce usable code size.

var g := rise_gravity * (fall_gravity_multiplier if velocity.y > 0.0 else 1.0)
    velocity.y = minf(velocity.y + g * delta, max_fall_speed)

beats.narration_text: Horizontal speed approaches a target rather than jumping instantly. Ground acceleration, braking, and air acceleration are separate choices. Multiply acceleration by delta when updating velocity; keep the final movement call responsible for displacement.

var rate := air_accel

    velocity.x = move_toward(velocity.x, axis * max_speed, rate * delta)

beats.narration_text: Coyote time permits a jump shortly after leaving a ledge. Jump buffering remembers a recent press before landing. They are different timer windows. Consume both when a jump starts so a held permission cannot launch another jump.

beats.narration_text: Releasing jump early reduces upward speed for a shorter hop. A stomp bounce sets a new upward velocity. If you author gravity yourself, area gravity overrides do not automatically replace that policy; decide how local gravity should contribute.

beats.narration_text: A rigid body asks the solver to calculate motion. Forces sustain a push; an impulse produces a one-time change. For this isolated example, mass two and impulse one hundred twenty predict a velocity change of sixty.

lecture.why: Exact runnable source is the teaching target; a full editor layout would reduce usable code size.

props.title: impulse · source excerpt
props.code:
rb.position=Vector2(380,300)
    rb.mass=2.0
    rb.gravity_scale=0.0
    rb.linear_damp=0.0
    rb.collision_layer=L.bit(L.DEBRIS);rb.collision_mask=L.bit(L.WORLD)
    rb.contact_monitor=true;rb.max_contacts_reported=4
    shape(rb,Vector2(70,70),Color("8b8f96"));stage.add_child(rb)
    await ticks(2)
    rb.apply_central_impulse(Vector2(120,0))
    await ticks(2)
    check("impulse changes velocity",absf(rb.linear_velocity.x-60)<1,rb.linear_velocity.x)

beats.narration_text: A force acts over time. An impulse represents a one-time momentum change. With the same impulse, doubling mass halves the ideal velocity change. Do not repeatedly apply a jump impulse every rendered frame; that changes the intended event into repeated pushes.

lecture.why: A labeled ideal model separates the continuous push from a discrete event

beats.narration_text: A rigid body can collide even when your script receives no contact signal. For body entered reporting, enable contact monitoring and allow enough reported contacts. Our crate fixture sets both and observes a floor contact. Reporting and physical response are separate concerns.

beats.narration_text: Physics ticks and rendered frames are different clocks. The default physics rate is sixty ticks per second. Run collision-based motion in physics callbacks and use delta. Correctly scaled render-frame motion still does not give the same collision scheduling.

lecture.why: The spatial or temporal transformation is the claim; a physical-object metaphor would obscure its exact geometry.

beats.narration_text: Speed divided by tick rate estimates travel per tick. It is not a collision theorem. Our character's swept movement detected a four-pixel floor across a requested three-hundred-pixel displacement. Method, shape, direction, and backend all matter.

beats.narration_text: For fast rigid bodies, continuous collision detection can reduce tunneling. Two D provides ray and shape modes; three D exposes its own settings. Also consider thicker collision geometry and a higher physics rate. None is a universal prevention guarantee.

lecture.why: A real captured artifact exists and directly supports the claim; reconstructed output would add no evidence.

beats.narration_text: Interpolation draws intermediate poses between physics states. It smooths presentation without simulating extra contacts. Temporarily testing at ten ticks per second makes mistakes obvious. Restore the intended rate and test pixel snapping and camera behavior together.

beats.narration_text: A respawn is a discontinuity. Set the new position, clear unwanted velocity, then reset physics interpolation. For a rigid body, change the simulated state through its integration callback. Frequent transform writes can fight the solver.

props.title: respawn · source excerpt
props.code:
func respawn(at: Vector2) -> void:
    global_position = at
    velocity = Vector2.ZERO
    reset_physics_interpolation()

beats.narration_text: A fixed timestep improves consistency, but it is not a promise of identical physics across runs, devices, or backends. Grade documented structure and behavior within tolerances. Exact replay requirements need a separate determinism design and validation plan.

beats.narration_text: Godot's two D and three D physics are separate systems. Jolt is now built into Godot and is the default for new projects in the checked documentation. Existing projects keep their selected backend; inspect the setting before interpreting behavior.
